title: If coding has been solved, why does software keep getting worse?
titleZh: 如果编码已经解决了，为什么软件却越来越糟糕？
author: pchm
relevanceReason: 命中 4 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: As I’m writing this, we’re in the middle of an AI-induced mass psychosis. People are literally token-maxxing themselves into hospital beds, scrambling to capture some of that market value before everything is automated away. I can’t blame them. Models keep getting better, programmers are being laid off left and right. We’ve been repeatedly told that AI will write 100% of the code by the end of the year. Whether that’s true or not, this may not be the best time to sit back. The widespread excitement around the Agentic Era comes with the promise of greater productivity and higher quality. There’s no denying that these new tools have already revolutionized how we create and use software. They have raised upper management’s expectations for team output. They may have upgraded the average skill set of software teams in a way we have not seen before. So why does software keep getting worse across the board? A few examples from last week alone:

My banking app requires, on average, three FaceID logins before the 3D Secure confirmation view appears. I opened Slack on macOS, the icon kept bouncing in the dock for a few seconds. I got impatient, switched to Ghostty, and started typing. Just then, the Slack window appeared, stole focus from Ghostty and the git pull command was sent to the group chat. My LG fridge started making weird sounds, so I tried to file a warranty claim, through a multi-step form with countless fields. It failed with a submission error at the very end. And I only found out because I looked at the JavaScript console. My car’s infotainment system got a software update recently. It was never great to begin with, but at least it didn’t reboot itself during every drive. Now, it’s riddled with bugs: the turn-signal sound randomly goes silent until I reboot the OS; I tap the screen to open Google Maps — the radio app shows up; there’s a 1-2-second lag before anything happens after I tap the screen. This is no longer just a UX problem at this point — those bugs affect your ability to focus on driving.

A few months ago, I saw a LinkedIn thread by a PM on the team that redesigned the car’s OS. They were congratulating themselves on what an amazing job they had done. I keep thinking about that post every time I have to fight their product.

While I can’t know the full story, I’m willing to bet that most of the teams behind those bugs have access to the latest models, with generous token budgets. LLMs can be really good at squashing bugs if given the chance. Software has always had bugs, and the nostalgia for the good old macOS Snow Leopard era when everything was stable is mostly the product of selective memory. Software may have been better back in the day, but that was mainly because it was much simpler. Since then, we have kept coming up with new abstractions, new frontend frameworks, and more infrastructure complexity. The bar for “user experience” has kept rising, but everything has become increasingly fragile. We’ve reached a point where an update to macOS — or to any app I rely on, really — is a source of dread rather than excitement. I now expect the new version to be worse. This isn’t a rant against AI. Those humming GPU farms have given us superpowers, but we still don’t use them to build better software. Software vendors have long been KPI-oriented, and making things more stable doesn’t always have a direct effect on the numbers. It doesn’t look exciting in presentations:

This quarter, we won’t be releasing any new features, and we have no plans to redesign anything — we will exclusively focus on fixing bugs. — Imaginary PM at a BigCo Until this attitude changes, the great software quality decay will continue. That doesn’t sound optimistic, but I’m actually excited about what comes next. As companies collectively spiral into AI debt, individual developers have a unique opportunity to build software that would previously have been beyond their reach. I have no hope for my car’s Android Auto or LG’s stupid website — but I choose to believe that everyday software will get better as a result of this frustration. We’re already seeing acts of rebellion against the current state of macOS and Windows, and I hope the trend will spread across the stack.

comments.author: mancerayder
comments.textRawHtml:
> We’ve reached a point where an update to macOS — or to any app I rely on, really — is a source of dread rather than excitement. I now expect the new version to be worse.

I actually relate to that. It used to be cool and exciting to update to see what new things are coming for free. I was just looking up what Fedora Workstation 45 might bring.

Updates on phones, TV's, cars and non-Linux operating systems on PC's/laptops are downright scary to me now. What will they add that I don't want? What more connectivity to the external world are they going to wire in?

MacOS lost everyone's trust by ruining the experience, but even before it happened that trying to resize a window makes it feel like life will be at 80 years-old, hunting a tiny invisible border, even before that there wasn't anything exciting.

What Microsoft I think did (and I can't prove it), before I moved off of Windows 11, was to bundle all changes in "required security updates." So you have no choice but to update (or go through special settings to turn it off, or just defer it), but when the machine comes back you have a new Welcome prompt to some new connectivity to something nefarious. AI features I never asked for, that's the most recent dark pattern here.
comments.textZhHtml:
> 我们已经到了这样一个地步：macOS（或者我真正依赖的任何应用程序）的更新让人感到恐惧而不是兴奋。我现在预计新版本会更糟。

我确实对此有感触。 过去，免费更新看看有哪些新东西即将推出是一件很酷又令人兴奋的事情。 我只是在寻找 Fedora Workstation 45 可能会带来什么。

手机、电视、汽车和 PC/笔记本电脑上的非 Linux 操作系统的更新现在对我来说非常可怕。 他们会添加哪些我不想要的内容？ 他们还要与外部世界建立更多的连接吗？

MacOS 通过破坏体验而失去了每个人的信任，但即使在尝试调整窗口大小让人感觉生活就像 80 岁时一样，寻找一个微小的看不见的边界，甚至在此之前也没有什么令人兴奋的事情发生之前，我认为 Microsoft 所做的（而且我无法证明），在我离开 Windows 11 之前，是将所有更改捆绑在“所需的安全性”中更新。” 因此，您别无选择，只能更新（或通过特殊设置将其关闭，或只是推迟它），但当机器回来时，您会看到一个新的欢迎提示，提示您与某些邪恶的东西有新的连接。 我从未要求过的人工智能功能，这是这里最新的黑暗模式。

children.author: xingped
children.textRawHtml: Yep, this 100%. When I see a "pending update" notification or icon somewhere, the first thing I think is "I don't want to update, they're just going to break something new". I _hate_ updates now. Doesn't matter what software it is, with the small exception of video games. (Except Dead By Daylight. Behavior, the devs, are the most hilariously incompetent devs on the planet, but at least their incompetence is confined to their own game.)
children.textZhHtml: 是的，这 100%。当我在某处看到“待更新”通知或图标时，我想到的第一件事是“我不想更新，他们只是要破坏新的东西”。我现在_讨厌_更新。无论是什么软件，除了视频游戏之外。 （《黎明杀机》除外。Behaviour 的开发者是这个星球上最无能的开发者，但至少他们的无能仅限于他们自己的游戏。）

children.author: djaro
children.textRawHtml: Maybe this is because video games can always add more features. Realistically, what useful feature could even be added to Word? I want to write text. It lets me write text. Program done. I dont see why Word would ever need an update other than maintenance or a security patch.
children.textZhHtml: 也许这是因为视频游戏总是可以添加更多功能。实际上，Word 中还可以添加哪些有用的功能？我想写文字。它让我可以写文字。程序完成了。我不明白为什么 Word 除了维护或安全补丁之外还需要更新。

children.author: zrobotics
children.textRawHtml:
The only software I've been excited about an update for in years has been games, that seems like the only category where devs actually add features people are excited about. For example, the latest KCD2 patch added a fun but brief new quest [0].

Not universal though. Besides your example, even for single player games patches can be basically malicious. I've had Fallout 4 locked on updates for like 3 years at this point, everything Bethesda has added has degraded the experience for zero upside. But I can't think of any software besides a game where I have been anything but dreading an update in years. Slack wants to update? Great, it'll probably break/degrade my work flow in some minor way, and they're one of the lesser offenders on my work machine.

[0] https://steamdb.info/patchnotes/23914554/
children.textZhHtml:
多年来我唯一对更新感到兴奋的软件是游戏，这似乎是开发人员真正添加人们感兴趣的功能的唯一类别。例如，最新的 KCD2 补丁添加了一个有趣但简短的新任务 [0]。

但不通用。除了你的例子之外，即使对于单人游戏补丁也可能基本上是恶意的。到目前为止，我已经将《辐射 4》锁定更新了大约 3 年，贝塞斯达添加的所有内容都降低了体验的零提升。但我想不出除了游戏之外还有什么软件能让我多年来一直害怕更新。 Slack 想要更新吗？太好了，它可能会在某种程度上破坏/降低我的工作流程，而且它们是我工作机器上较轻的罪犯之一。

[0] https://steamdb.info/patchnotes/23914554/

children.author: DiskoHexyl
children.textRawHtml:
Lots of games’ updates break popular mods, introduce launchers and/or break linux compatibility and/or online mode, remove music with expired licenses, censor something and increase system requirements.

Sadly we’re way past the point where games became like all the other software in that regard
children.textZhHtml:
许多游戏的更新破坏了流行的模组，引入启动器和/或破坏Linux兼容性和/或在线模式，删除许可证过期的音乐，审查某些内容并增加系统要求。

可悲的是，我们已经过了游戏在这方面变得像所有其他软件一样的阶段

children.author: bee_rider
children.textRawHtml:
I think games are the exception because they are

* relatively small purchases

* paid for directly by the user

* expected to be enjoyable

Most other software fails at least one of those tests, reducing the ability to shop around and make an informed decision.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为游戏是个例外，因为它们

*相对较小的购买量

*由用户直接支付

*预计会带来乐趣

大多数其他软件至少无法通过其中一项测试，从而降低了货比三家并做出明智决定的能力。

children.author: madeofpalk
children.textRawHtml:
> * paid for directly by the user

hahahahah. Games are steering further and further to this not being true. Where each player explicitly doesn't pay for it, and instead they contain an increasing series of dark patterns in order to steer players to fleece their money in a series of microtransactions.
children.textZhHtml:
> * 由用户直接付费

哈哈哈哈。游戏正在朝着越来越不真实的方向发展。每个玩家都明确不为此付费，而是包含越来越多的黑暗模式，以引导玩家通过一系列微交易来骗取金钱。

children.author: bee_rider
children.textRawHtml: You have a good point, there are some games with terrible business models too. I just don’t play them, haha.
children.textZhHtml: 你的观点很好，但也有一些游戏的商业模式很糟糕。我就是不玩，哈哈。

children.author: classified
children.textRawHtml: We can't change the fact that commercial OS vendors are all feudal overlords now, but the lawmakers are letting them get away with it and that is something we might still be able to change.
children.textZhHtml: 我们无法改变商业操作系统厂商现在都是封建霸主的事实，但立法者却让他们逍遥法外，这是我们仍然可以改变的。

children.author: mancerayder
children.textRawHtml: KCD2 is number 1 of a small number of updates I am excited about.
children.textZhHtml: KCD2 是令我兴奋的少数更新中的第 1 个。

children.author: formerly_proven
children.textRawHtml: I really look forward to new Fedora releases.
children.textZhHtml: 我真的很期待新的 Fedora 版本。

children.author: benoau
children.textRawHtml: I really look forward to Pop OS updates... but it's because they broke a bunch of stuff and stripped most apps down to their basics.
children.textZhHtml: 我真的很期待 Pop OS 更新...但这是因为它们破坏了很多东西，并将大多数应用程序剥离到了基础。

children.author: dosisking
children.textRawHtml: I dread Linux kernel updates. Still running a 4.4 era kernel. Kernel versions have always been hit or miss, some are good, others introduced a new bug. Sometimes it's necessary to upgrade glibc as well which is a huge pain.
children.textZhHtml: 我害怕 Linux 内核更新。仍然运行 4.4 时代的内核。内核版本总是时好时坏，有些是好的，有些则引入了新的错误。有时还需要升级 glibc，这是一个巨大的痛苦。

children.author: worthless-trash
children.textRawHtml: What a target rich environment for attackers.
children.textZhHtml: 对于攻击者来说，这是一个目标丰富的环境。

children.author: lokar
children.textRawHtml: I remember when OS vendors shipped à la carte patches.  You could pick the ones you wanted (to some extent).
children.textZhHtml: 我记得操作系统供应商发布了点菜补丁。  您可以选择您想要的（在某种程度上）。

children.author: chii
children.textRawHtml:
you can still do it: https://www.catalog.update.microsoft.com/Search.aspx?q=windo...

hopefully it doesn't get removed.
children.textZhHtml:
您仍然可以这样做：https://www.catalog.update.microsoft.com/Search.aspx?q=windo...

希望它不会被删除。

children.author: inigyou
children.textRawHtml: Factorio or Minecraft change things every update.
children.textZhHtml: Factorio 或 Minecraft 每次更新都会改变一些东西。

children.author: xingped
children.textRawHtml: I don't play those, but I know at least with games like those, where players like to play on specific versions, there's usually ways to stay on a specific version without too much hassle.
children.textZhHtml: 我不玩这些游戏，但我至少知道，对于这类游戏，玩家喜欢玩特定版本，通常有方法可以轻松地留在特定版本上。

children.author: herbst
children.textRawHtml:
I stopped with Microsoft buying minecraft. But before that they didn't change but add things.

I can't remember a single time I was disappointed because something changed.
children.textZhHtml:
我停止了微软收购我的世界。但在此之前，他们没有改变，而是添加了一些东西。

我不记得有一次因为某些事情发生了变化而感到失望。
